caption: [Community Centre Staff Commended For Saving A Life]On 29 April, three staff members of Boon Lay Community Centre (CC) Ms Gayathiri d/o Selvam, Mr Mohammad Imraan s/o Noor Abdul Kadir Jailaini and Ms Lee May Kay Peggy were on duty when they were approached by a member of the public informing them that someone had collapsed at the CCs multi-purpose hall.Ms Gayathiri and Mr Imraan rushed to the scene and saw the patient lying unresponsive on the floor. Mr Imraan immediately called 995 while Ms Gayathiri ran back to her office to retrieve an Automated External Defibrillator (AED). She returned with Ms Lee, who prepared the AED for use while Ms Gayathiri began CPR.Soon, Ms Jeane Fong Jin Yi, Boon Lay Constituency Director, arrived and contacted the patients family member. Upon using the AED, the patient began showing signs of breathing. The team then continued several more cycles of CPR, as advised by the AED.As a result of the teams timely response and teamwork, they were able to successfully resuscitate the patient prior to SCDFs arrival. The patient survived and is alive today.On 22 May 2025, the four individuals were presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by SAC Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division.You too can make a difference during an emergency by downloading the SCDF myResponder app and registering as a Community First Responder via the app. You can also learn essential lifesaving skills through SCDFs Responders Plus Programme at go.gov.sg/scdfrpp. Lets build ANationOfLifesavers together!CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRole

caption: [SCDF Day @ Civil Defence Academy]Yesterday evening, the SCDF Day Dining-In ceremony was held at the Civil Defence Academy. This annual event commemorates the integration of the Singapore Fire Service and SCDF on 15 April 1989, consolidating Singapores fire, rescue and emergency medical services response into a single organisation.The ceremony, which serves as a platform for our officers to rededicate their commitment to our lifesaving mission and reaffirm our core values of Pride and Care, was attended by SCDF regular officers, full-time National Servicemen, Operationally Ready National Servicemen and civilian staff. Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS), Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, graced the event as the Guest of Honour. In his speech, MOS Faishal recognised and commended SCDF personnel who have exemplified SCDFs core values in and beyond their duties. He also spoke about SCDFs Operation Lionheart contingent, who were recently deployed to Myanmar for disaster relief efforts, and praised the team for their professionalism, compassion and dedication to saving lives. Congratulations to all award winners! As we honour their achievements, we also reaffirm our dedication and commitment towards our mission to protect and save lives and property. caption: [Update 9: Operation Lionhearts Homecoming] Earlier today (8 April) at about 4pm, the SCDFs Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent returned to Singapore. The OLH contingent, comprising 80 members and four search canines, was deployed to support search and rescue efforts in Myanmar on 29 March, a day after the country was hit by the devastating earthquake. A welcome reception was held at Changi Airport, where Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law, and Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development received the contingent members. Families and loved ones were also present to warmly welcome them home. In his welcome address, Minister Shanmugam expressed his heartfelt gratitude to the OLH contingent, along with officers from the Home Team Science and Technology Agency (HTX), for assisting with search and rescue operations in Myanmar. He commended the contingent for their dedication to service. Minister Shanmugam also expressed his appreciation to the families and loved ones of the contingent members for their support. To our OLH contingent, you have truly embodied the spirit of being a Lifesaver, not only in Singapore but also beyond borders. Welcome home, our Lifesavers We would like to express our utmost appreciation to the Singapore Embassy in Yangon for facilitating the OLH contingents deployment in Myanmar. We would also like to thank Singapore Airlines, Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore, Changi Airport Group, Myanmar Airways International, ST Logistics and SATS Ltd Singapore Hub team for facilitating the contingents flight and logistical arrangements on short notice. The people of Myanmar will always be in our hearts and minds. Though the road to recovery may be challenging, their admirable resilience in the face of adversity will guide them through, and we are confident that they will emerge stronger and recover from this disaster.

caption: [Update 8: Stand down of Operation Lionheart in Myanmar] The 80-member Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent has begun preparations to return home. Over the last two days, the OLH contingent has been handing over essential supplies such as tents, canned food and ready-to-eat rations, to the Myanmar Fire Services Department (MFSD). The OLH contingent also donated two tents to Naypyidaw Womens Hospital, and five tents along with medical drugs and medical supplies to Naypyidaw General Hospital. It is hoped that these supplies will continue to help the relief and recovery efforts as the people of Myanmar work to rebuild their community. On behalf of SCDF, Team Leader COL Tay Zhi Wei, gifted a battery-operated hydraulic cutter to U Myat Thu, Director General MFSD. This cutter was instrumental in rescuing a man trapped underneath concrete slabs in a semi-collapsed three-storey residential building on 30 March. Despite its compact size, the cutters powerful capability enabled it to cut through the rebar in the concrete slabs within an extremely confined area, freeing the man and saving his life. This cutter is now an enduring symbol of friendship between the SCDF and MFSD, where it will continue to serve, saving lives in the good hands of MFSD. An appreciation ceremony organised by the National Disaster Management Committee (NDMC) in Naypyidaw, brought together Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) teams from Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapore, Vietnam and Philippines. A moment of silence was observed in memory of the earthquake victims. The OLH contingent will be returning home tomorrow (8 April) at 4:10pm, on Singapore Airlines at Changi Airport Terminal 3.

caption: [Update 7: Operation Lionheart Search Operations and Medical Care in Naypyidaw]Over the past two days, the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent has been actively involved in search operations in Ottara Thiri Township, Naypyidaw.At a partially-collapsed nine-storey hotel, the OLH contingent conducted a joint risk assessment with the Myanmar Earthquake Relief Contingent from Vietnam before commencing search operations. After an extensive search effort, a body was discovered beneath layers of concrete and steel. The OLH contingent worked with Indonesias National Search and Rescue Agency (BASARNAS) to recover the body by breaking through the debris.In addition to the search operations, the OLH contingent also established medical outposts in Pyokkon and Dhakhinna Thiri Townships to provide medical care to locals affected by the disaster. The medical outposts were set up at a monastery in Pyokkon and on the open ground of a hotel in Dhakhinna Thiri Township. The OLH contingents doctors and paramedics, assisted by the rescuers, provided wound care to promote healing and prevent infection. They also attended to patients experiencing acute post-earthquake symptoms such as dizziness as well as musculoskeletal issues which were aggravated by carrying heavy loads while seeking refuge from the earthquake.Since the OLH contingents arrival in Naypyidaw on 29 March, they have searched a total of 26 sites and provided medical care to approximately 130 local residents affected by the disaster.

caption: [SCDFs Operation Lionheart Deployment to Myanmar]In response to the request for humanitarian assistance in the aftermath of an earthquake in Myanmar yesterday (28 Mar), SCDF has deployed the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent to assist in disaster rescue efforts. The contingent departed from Changi Airport at about 1:20pm today (29 Mar).Led by Team Leader, COL Tay Zhi Wei, the 80-member OLH contingent comprises rescuers from the elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), Operationally Ready National Servicemen (ORNS), full-time National Servicemen medical doctors, paramedics, search specialists with four canines, hazardous materials specialists, and support officers. The pre-departure briefing and preparation began early this morning at HQ SCDF. The OLH contingent is carrying an array of portable Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) equipment such as cutting, breaking and lifting equipment, as well as life detection devices and fibre-optic scopes. These equipment which are battery operated will allow the team to be swiftly deployed to affected areas to begin immediate USAR operations. In addition, three SCDF officers are also deployed to Myanmar as part of the ASEAN Emergency Response and Assessment Team (ERAT) under the auspices of the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on Disaster Management (AHA Centre). The ASEAN-ERATs primary function is to provide rapid assessment and determine the critical resources required for the areas affected by the earthquake. Prior to the contingents departure, Associate Professor , Minister of State, Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development met with the team at HQ SCDF to express his appreciation to the officers and to see them off, together with their family and loved ones.We would like to thank for facilitating the flight arrangements on short notice, especially during such major disasters where prompt assistance is crucial to those in need. We would also like to thank and SATS Ltd Singapore Hub team for their assistance.We wish our OLH contingent a safe and successful mission.

caption: [Responders, Partners and Volunteers Appreciation Event 2025]On Tuesday (18 Feb), the Responders, Partners and Volunteers Appreciation Event was held at HomeTeamNS Khatib.The event, jointly organised by the Ministry of Home Affairs and SCDF, recognises SGSecure Responders, SCDF Community First Responders (CFRs) and SCDF volunteers who have helped save lives and property, as well as community partners who have played a significant role in building the pool of Responders.Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State (MOS), Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, graced the event as the Guest of Honour.In his speech, MOS Faishal highlighted the Lifesavers Emergency Point (LEP) initiative, a joint effort between SCDF, Temasek Foundation, the Housing Development Board and Town Councils, in strengthening the communitys readiness towards emergencies. Situated at the lift lobbies of HDB blocks, these LEPs are equipped with Automated External Defibrillators and fire extinguishers for public use. Since 2023, over 4,000 fire extinguishers have been installed across one in every two HDB blocks. These fire extinguishes have already been used in more than 70 minor fire incidents.During the event, 27 Responders received appreciation plaques for their contributions towards saving lives. 52 community partners, including all 17 Town Councils, were recognised for their partnership with the Home Team to strengthen emergency preparedness initiatives. 26 SCDF Volunteers comprising Civil Defence Auxiliary Unit Exemplary Officers, National Civil Defence Cadet Corps Honorary Officers and Senior Cadet Lieutenants as well as Civil Defence Lionhearter Clubs were also presented appreciation plaques for their dedication and efforts.Thank you to all our Responders, volunteers and community partners! We look forward to the continued collaboration in empowering the community to step forward to help during emergencies.CommunityFirstResponderCommunityLifesaversANationofLifesaversOurCFRsOurHeroesWhatsYourRoleSGSecure

Premises owners are reminded to practice good housekeeping and adhere to the fire safety regulations, so as to ensure the safety of everyone.

caption: [Fire @ Block 612, Ang Mo Kio Avenue 4]Earlier this morning at 1:55am, SCDF was alerted to the fire at the abovementioned location.Firefighters from Ang Mo Kio Fire Station, supported by Bishan Fire Station, entered the smoke-filled unit on the 11th floor to fight the fire. The fire, which involved a bedroom, was extinguished with a water jet. As a result of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and soot damage. 5 persons from the affected unit had evacuated prior to SCDFs arrival. SCDF conveyed two persons to Singapore General Hospital and two persons to KK Womens and Childrens Hospital for smoke inhalation. Another person declined to be sent to hospital. About 30 residents from the block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the cause of the fire is of electrical origin, likely from an electrical socket in the bedroom.The cause of the fire is under investigation. SCDF would like to remind the public on good practices to prevent electrical fires from occurring: a) Do not overload electrical sockets with electrical appliances; b) Switch off electrical appliances when not in use; c) Check for frayed wires or cracked cords. If observed, the electrical appliance should be repaired or replaced. Do not use faulty appliances; d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces; e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. He was assessed by a paramedic and conveyed to Tan Tock Seng Hospital as a precautionary measure. The cause of the fire is under investigation.

caption: [1st International Rota Commander Course Graduation Ceremony]Earlier this evening, 65 cadets graduated from SCDFs first International Rota Commander Course (I-RCC) at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA).The graduating cohort, comprising cadets from the Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority (ADCDA) , have spent the last 6 months undergoing a comprehensive training programme to acquire the necessary skills and knowledge to perform the role of frontline commanders.The I-RCC follows the same training and assessment framework as SCDFs Rota Commander Course, with the cadets undergoing training in areas such as firefighting, medical training, urban search and rescue, and hazardous materials mitigation operations. Upon graduation, the cadets will continue their training at the Abu Dhabi Police Academy, before commissioning as Senior Officers of the ADCDA.Present at the ceremony were H.E. Mr Jamal Abdulla AlSuwaidi, Ambassador of the United Arab Emirates to Singapore, and H.E. Brigadier General Salem Abdullah Bin Barak Al Dhaheri, Director General (DG), Abu Dhabi Civil Defence Authority. A day before the ceremony, DG Salem visited CDA and Home Team Tactical Centre (HTTC) to tour the training facilities and see firsthand the training that the cadets had undergone. Congratulations to the 1st I-RCC graduates! We wish you all the best as you move on to the next phase of your lifesaving journey

caption: [Mass Fire Evacuation Drill Closing Ceremony 2023] Yesterday (26 Sep), CDG ZIG Holdings Pte Ltd hosted the annual Mass Fire Evacuation Drill (MFED) closing ceremony at their premises. caption: [Elevating Training, Learning and Development - SCDF's Workplan Seminar 2023]SCDF's Workplan Seminar (WPS) 2023 was held yesterday (31 Jul), where more than 300 guests were in attendance at the Civil Defence Academy (CDA). Mr K Shanmugam, Minister for Home Affairs and Minister for Law graced the event as our Guest-of-Honour. Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development was also present at the WPS, along with representatives from international fire departments. In line with this year's WPS theme of "Elevating Training, Learning and Development", the seminar showcased how we will be preparing our officers for future challenges through our redeveloped Field Training Area (FTA). One of the centrepiece of the FTAs is the National Emergency Medical Services Training Centre, which is built to replicate the real-world pre-hospital emergency care environment. This helps our EMS responders train for diverse emergencies from onsite medical intervention to end-to-end clinical care. The redeveloped FTA also comprises the Fire Research Centre, which is a purpose-built environment for burn testing and enhanced fire modelling capability to aid SCDF in developing improved firefighting techniques. These are two of the seven purpose-built facilities at CDA that will offer enhanced learning and training realism for emergency responders.The third and final phase of CDA's redevelopment will entail the refitting of new fire simulators in our nine-storey furnace building. Phase three is targeted to be ready by next year. SCDFworkplan2023

caption: [Fire @ Blk 618 Bedok Reservoir Road] Early this morning (21 July) at about 3:40am, SCDF was alerted to a fire at the abovementioned location. Upon SCDF's arrival, black smoke was seen emitting from a unit on the 7th floor. Donned with breathing apparatuses, firefighters quickly entered the smoke-logged unit to fight the fire. The fire, which involved a bedroom and part of the living room, was extinguished by SCDF with a water jet. Due to the intense heat of the fire, the rest of the unit sustained heat and smoke damage. Two persons had evacuated the affected unit before SCDF's arrival. Both were assessed by an SCDF paramedic for smoke inhalation. One of them was conveyed to the Singapore General Hospital and the other declined to be sent to the hospital. About 90 residents from the affected block were evacuated by the Police and SCDF as a precautionary measure. Preliminary investigation indicates that the fire was caused by an electrical origin in the affected bedroom.*Fire Safety Tips:*SCDF would like to remind the public on some good practices to adopt in the household to prevent electrical fires from occurring:a) Never overload electrical outlets with electrical appliances;b) Always switch off electrical appliances when not in use;c) Check the condition of wires regularly. Wires that are frayed or cracked should be replaced or repaired immediately;d) Do not run wires under carpets or mats and keep wires away from hot surfaces;e) Use appliances and electrical plugs bearing the Safety Mark. The categories of appliances can be found at ; f) Do not leave batteries or devices charging unattended for an extended period of time or overnight.

caption: [27th Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Parade]Yesterday, 48 Officer Cadets from the 27th Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as Senior Officers at the Civil Defence Academy. Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim, Deputy Chairperson, Government Parliamentary Committee (Home Affairs & Law), graced the event as the Guest-of-Honour.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of Officer Cadets into Senior Officers after a 28-week residential course. During the course, the Officer Cadets, comprising both Regular Officers, Full-time National Servicemen as well as international trainees hailing from Bahrain and Vietnam, were equipped with the requisite operational skills and knowledge to perform the role of frontline commanders.The 27th RCC is also the first batch of Officer Cadets to include nine Direct-Entry Paramedic Senior Officers. Prior to joining the 27th RCC, the nine Paramedic Officer Cadets went through a 12-month paramedicine training course at Nanyang Polytechnic and a three month operational attachment at the frontline fire stations. The SCDF Paramedic Senior Officer scheme underscores the transformation of SCDFs Emergency Medical Services (EMS) to meet increasing operational demands while further elevating the service delivery of our EMS to the public.In speaking to the graduating cadets, Mr Zhulkarnain emphasised the importance of leadership, responsibility and upholding high operational standards while carrying out their respective lifesaving roles and responsibilities. He also underlined the need to uphold the hard-earned public trust which generations of SCDF officers have worked hard to nurture, through professionalism, commitment, and dedication to serving the public.Congratulations to the 27th RCC! We look forward to their contributions in the Life Saving Force Pic 1,3: CPL Gao Wei Jie, Civil Defence Academy Pic 2,4-10: CPL Goh Rhy Yan, Civil Defence Academy

caption: [Update 2: Collapsed Structure Incident Along Bernam Street]Following an intensive search operation, a worker who was earlier reported missing, was sighted to be pinned under the collapsed reinforced concrete structure around 1800hrs. The worker had no pulse and breathing. The SCDF immediately conducted cutting and breaking operations to free the casualty. The operation also required the Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) personnel to dig their way through the rubble to create space and assess where parts of the body may have been trapped. This was further complicated due to the weight of the concrete slab which was in excess of 50 tonnes (estimated) as well as mangled scaffolding around the body. The casualty was finally freed after nearly four hours around 2145hrs. He was pronounced dead at the scene by a paramedic. Earlier in the search operation, CCTV footages from the surrounding buildings were obtained by the Police to assist in the assessment of the situation. A fibre optic scope, life detection equipment and search canines were also deployed to detect for signs of life. The operation involved the coordinated use of heavy machinery from the construction site as well as rescue equipment to cut and lift the reinforced concrete slab. 11 SCDF emergency vehicles and about 70 personnel, including rescuers from the DART were deployed at the scene for this operation.

caption: [Four Gurkha Contingent Officers Commended for Saving the Life of a Cardiac Arrest Victim] On 25 Mar 2023, at about 11:30 a.m., four officers from Gurkha Contingent (GC) of the were driving in the vicinity of Woodlands Industrial Park, where they saw a man lying motionless by the roadside of Woodlands Industrial Park D Street 1. Team Leader Senior Staff Sergeant (SSS) Man Kumar Limbu and Operator Corporal (CPL) Dinesh Limbu quickly approached the unconscious man and found him in a state of cardiac arrest. SSS Man Kumar immediately called for an ambulance and directed CPL Dinesh and Operator CPL Jeevan Gharti Magar to perform cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on the man. At the same time, Deputy Team Leader Sergeant (SGT) Sabin Gurung managed the oncoming traffic for the safety of the man and the officers rendering CPR. The officers continued with the CPR on the unconscious man until the arrival of an SCDF ambulance. As a result of the prompt and timely lifesaving actions by the GC officers, the man is recovering well today. Yesterday (17 May), the four officers were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award. The awards were presented by Colonel Goh Boon Han, Commander, 4th SCDF Division. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder (CFR) via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted of nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. Being trained in basic firefighting, first aid and CPR is useful but not mandatory to qualify as a CFR! Anyone who is willing can do something to help . The SCDF values the strong friendship and bonds forged with our Trkiye counterparts during the deployment. The people of Trkiye have demonstrated admirable resilience and fortitude, and we are confident they would emerge much stronger as they rebuild their lives and homes." - Commissioner Eric Yap, Commissioner SCDF

caption: [Exercise Northstar XI @ Jurong Island] Earlier today, Exercise Northstar XI (XNS11) was held at Jurong Island to validate multi-agency emergency response plans and hone coordination among national agencies. More than 300 personnel from SCDF, various key government agencies and industry partners participated in the exercise. The XNS11 began with an armed adversary scenario and a sea interdiction response, where the perpetrators were jointly neutralised by SAFs Island Defence Task Force and SPFs Ground Response Force, Emergency Response Team, and Police Coast Guard. Albeit that the perpetrators were neutralised, improvised explosive devices planted on Jurong Island were detonated remotely causing a chemical pipeline rupture and two oil tank fires. These scenarios were mitigated with the response of SCDF resources, among which were the HazMat Control Vehicle, HazMat Mitigation Vehicle, and SCDFs latest Modular Oil Tank Firefighting System. Mr Lee Hsien Loong, Prime Minister (PM) of Singapore, together with Cabinet members, were present to observe the exercise. In speaking to the media after the exercise, PM Lee reaffirmed the importance of inter-agency response during major emergencies to safeguard Singapores national security. In pursuing our shared mission of a safe and secure Singapore, XNS11 was an enriching opportunity for SCDF to work alongside other agencies to test and validate the Whole-of-Government response framework in the event of major crises and potential threat scenarios. Check out the photos to see what transpired during XNS11!XNS11ANationofLifesavers

Without hesitation, he called 995 and proceeded to extinguish the fire with a fire extinguisher that was in the centralised rubbish chute room. In a separate incident on 10 Feb 2023 at about 5:20 p.m., Mr Raymond Lim Koon Siang was on his way to fetch his child from school when he saw smoke coming out from a 2nd floor unit at Block 663 Choa Chu Kang Crescent. Instinctively, Mr Raymond dashed to retrieve a fire extinguisher from his truck which was parked nearby, and rushed to the affected unit. He entered the unit and extinguished the fire involving the kitchen stove and cabinet. Yesterday (28 Feb), the two members of public were presented with the SCDF Community First Responder Award for their civic-minded actions. The awards were presented by COL Bob Tan, Deputy Director, Volunteer and Community Partnership Department. You too can help by downloading the SCDFs myResponder app and register as a Community First Responder via the app. Through the app, you can be alerted to nearby emergencies such as a cardiac arrest incident or minor fires that can be quickly attended to by members of the public who are in the vicinity. caption: [Update 14: Standing down of Operation Lionheart]As Operation Lionheart (OLH) draws to a close, the 68-member contingent is preparing to depart from Trkiye later today (17 Feb). A few days prior to the departure, the OLH contingent met with the Trkiye National Medical Rescue Team, otherwise known as the Ulusal Medikal Kurtarma Ekibi (UMKE). The UMKE specialises in medical disaster relief and has been rendering assistance to Trkiye following the massive earthquake. During the meeting, the OLH contingent contributed medical supplies such as trauma equipment and medical drugs, as well as other necessities like food rations, thermal wear and tents.Ambassador Jonathan Tow, Ambassador Extraordinary and Plenipotentiary of the Republic of Singapore to the Republic of Trkiye also visited the OLH contingent at their Base of Operation as the OLH contingent were making preparations to stand down. The Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) suit worn by the OLH contingent represents an important element of identity among us and our commitment to saving lives. The USAR suits were presented to the locals as a gesture of our friendship and solidarity with them as they move forward to rebuild their lives following this devastating earthquake. Although the OLH contingent is leaving Trkiye, the people of Trkiye will always be in our hearts and minds

caption: [Update 13: SCDF's Operation Lionheart Psychological Team]A disaster can trigger critical stress. This can come in the form of emotional, mental or physical exhaustion, which can potentially be traumatic to responders who are deployed to disaster sites to undertake rescue operations.For the first time, two officers from the SCDFs Emergency Behavioural Sciences and Care unit (EBSC) formed part of the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent to provide in-situ psychological support to its responders.They monitor the contingent members morale and psychological well-being, and ensure the overall psychological readiness of rescuers during the deployment. These officers help enable appropriate and timely psychological intervention when required.Meet Home Team Specialist (HTS) Khoo Swee Giang, Lead Psychologist and LTA Khoo Chong Wee, Emergency Readiness Officer from SCDFs EBSC unit.

caption: [Update 10: SCDFs Search Platoon at Operation Lionheart]As part of the Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent, search specialists and four canines from SCDFs search platoon are deployed together with DART rescuers to conduct search and rescue operations at potential rescue sites.Highly intelligent, SCDFs search canines have the aptitude for searching for survivors in the rubble of collapsed buildings. With a keen sense of smell, they are trained to search confined spaces in collapsed building structures.To ensure the well-being of our four search canines, a series of measures are in place to ensure that they receive the best care during the deployment. This includes housing them in climate-controlled cargo holds during their flight, taking them on walks for playtime, providing them a nutritious diet and giving them a wipe-down at the end of the day to keep them clean. The search canines also have their own thermal jackets and blankets to keep them warm. In addition, the two medical doctors with the OLH contingent are also trained in basic canine care.Meet Timmy, Jack, Rizzo and Frenchy.

caption: [Update 7: Operation Lionheart Base of Operations in Kahramanmara]Following the arrival of the second Operation Lionheart (OLH) team in Adana, Trkiye on 10 Feb, the OLH Base of Operation (BoO) in Kahramanmara was expanded to accommodate the full 68-member OLH contingent.Over the last 24 hours, two teams from the OLH contingent were deployed at two different sectors in the city centre. Located about 13 km from the BoO, both teams conducted assessments and identified potential rescue sites. Each team comprised eight officers from DART, two search specialists with their canines, one paramedic and two support officers. USAR life detection equipment were also deployed to locate possible casualties for these sector assessments. A total of seven sites were assessed and both teams returned back to the BoO after the OLH contingents assistance were no longer required.

caption: [Update 5: Joint Rescue Operation at Kanldere Cd., Dulkadirolu/Kahramanmara, Trkiye]Yesterday at about 8 p.m. (10 Feb, 1 a.m., Singapore time), the advance team from SCDFs Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent was dispatched together with the Local Emergency Management Agency (LEMA) to conduct a search and rescue operation at Kanldere Cd., after reports of faint calls for help were heard coming from a semi-collapse 2-storey building.Upon arrival at the location, five elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) personnel and a paramedic worked closely with LEMA to conduct the search and rescue operation.After ensuring the stability of the semi-collapsed building, LEMA and SCDF accessed the second floor through the back of the building where the faint calls were heard. SCDF used a fibre-optic scope and confirmed that a man was trapped behind a large concrete slab. LEMA then used breaking equipment to create an opening. The man was rescued within half an hour.Throughout this operation, LEMA and SCDF were in constant contact with the trapped man. He was brought down from the building and was attended to by the locals.
cleaned_caption: [Update 5: Joint Rescue Operation at Kanldere Cd., Dulkadirolu/Kahramanmara, Trkiye] Yesterday at about 8 p.m. (10 Feb, 1 a.m., Singapore time), the advance team from SCDF's Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent was dispatched together with the Local Emergency Management Agency (LEMA) to conduct a search and rescue operation at Kanldere Cd., after reports of faint calls for help were heard coming from a semi-collapse 2-storey building. Upon arrival at the location, five elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART) personnel and a paramedic worked closely with LEMA to conduct the search and rescue operation. After ensuring the stability of the semi-collapsed building, LEMA and SCDF accessed the second floor through the back of the building where the faint calls were heard. SCDF used a fibre-optic scope and confirmed that a man was trapped behind a large concrete slab. LEMA then used breaking equipment to create an opening. The man was rescued within half an hour. Throughout this operation, LEMA and SCDF were in constant contact with the trapped man. He was brought down from the building and was attended to by the locals.

caption: [Update 4: SCDF Deploys Second Team to Trkiye]A second team, comprising 48 SCDF personnel and four canines from SCDF's K-9 unit, will depart for Adana, Trkiye at about 2 a.m. tomorrow morning (10 Feb). This team will augment the 20-member advance team that was deployed earlier this week. The 68-member strong Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent will give more scope, scale and capacity to carry out sustained and prolonged Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) operations within affected areas. To support the contingents enhanced USAR operations, additional search and rescue equipment, medical supplies, and communications and logistics support equipment, will also be brought along. The contingent was sent off by His Excellency Mehmet Burin Gnenli, Turkish Ambassador to Singapore, and Associate Professor Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development, at SCDF Headquarters earlier this evening.More updates on OLH operations will be provided over the next few days.

caption: [Basic Rescue Training Passing Out Parade - 166th Intake]Yesterday, 324 recruits from the 166th Intake stood proudly before their families and loved ones in a Passing Out Parade (POP) to mark the completion of their Basic Rescue Training (BRT) at the Civil Defence Academy. Equipped with essential lifesaving skills including the use of various rescue equipment and techniques, these recruits will now progress into the various vocational training courses in SCDF.The POP was officiated by DC Daniel Seet, Deputy Commissioner (Operations and Resilience). In his opening address, DC Daniel commended the recruits for their effort and commitment in completing the BRT, and wished them all the best as they embark on the next phase of their National Service (NS) journey. He also thanked the families and loved ones for their unwavering support in the recruits' NS journey. Our heartiest congratulations to the recruits of the 166th Intake! You have officially become Rescuers of the Life Saving Force . We look forward to your service and contributions in keeping Singapore safe and secure.ANationofLifesavers

caption: [Update 4 - Operation Lionheart (OLH) Deployment at New South Wales]The OLH Contingent Team A arrived at Condobolin town yesterday (20 Nov). After being briefed on the flood situation, the team was deployed to the sand banks near the river and lake to assist in setting up flood barriers to reduce floodwater damage to the local communities. Working closely with officers from the Australian Defence Force, Team A continued with their flood barrier operation today (21 Nov) at Condobolin town. Team B in Wagga Wagga city was redeployed to Deniliquin town earlier today. The team was deployed to assist in securing a hazardous debris (shipping container) that was drifting dangerously in the floodwaters. Working together with officers from and , the team did a quick assessment of the water conditions and managed to safely secure the shipping container to a concrete structure, and prevent it from drifting further into the main water stream. Team B was also subsequently deployed to deliver flood protection supplies to residences in the community, and assisted to set up flood protection for some of the residences together with the officers from the . Team A will be proceeding back to Parkes town while Team B will be stationed at Deniliquin town to provide further assistance as major flooding is expected in the area.

caption: [Update 3 - SCDF Operation Lionheart (OLH) Mission to New South Wales]Yesterday evening (18 Nov), the OLH contingent, which was split into two teams i.e. Team A and Team B, arrived at Parkes town and Wagga Wagga city respectively. Earlier today (19 Nov), Team A commenced search operations at Forbes town, which is about 30km away from Parkes town. The team rendered assistance to electricians who were working in a flooded area to reinstate power supply at a power station. Following operations at Forbes town, Team A will be proceeding to Condobolin town for their next deployment. Team B in Wagga Wagga city is on standby for activation as the situation there is dynamic, with an incoming storm anticipated. While on standby, the team practised their lifesaving and boat handling techniques at the nearby Wiradjuri Reserve.Lets give our best wishes to the OLH contingent and pen your words of encouragement for them in the comments section

caption: [Update 2 - SCDF Operation Lionheart Mission to New South Wales]The 16-member Operation Lionheart (OLH) contingent arrived at New South Wales (NSW) yesterday (17 Nov) and attended a pre-operations briefing at the NSW State Emergency Service (SES) Bankstown Unit where they were given an update of the flood situation by NSW SES officers. The contingent members were also given a quick familiarisation on the various equipment used by our counterparts at the NSW SES, such as the Inflatable Rescue Boat and the Reach and Rescue Pole.Later today, the OLH contingent will be split into two 7-member teams. The teams will be travelling to Parkes Town and Wagga Wagga City respectively, to prepare for search and rescue operations scheduled to commence on Saturday (19 Nov).LTC Lok Wee Keong, the Commander of SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance, and CPT Tan Chun Hui, Operation Support Officer, will be travelling to NSW SES Headquarters at Wollongong city where they will work with their counterparts NSW SES officers to oversee and coordinate the search and rescue operations at both flood sites.We wish our OLH contingent the best in their upcoming mission. Stay tuned for further updates on the OLH operations in the next few days.

caption: [SCDF Operation Lionheart Mission to New South Wales]A 16-member SCDF contingent departed for New South Wales, Australia at about 9:00 p.m. today (16 Nov). The contingent, led by LTC Lok Wee Keong, the commander of SCDFs elite Disaster Assistance and Rescue Team (DART), was deployed in support of the flood rescue efforts being conducted by the Fire and Rescue New South Wales. Supporting LTC Lok are DART officers LTA Sabree Dusuki and LTA Ahmad Faizal, who each have more than 25 years of operational experience in DART. The contingent is also augmented by an operations support officer and 12 DART officers with advanced lifesaver skills, powered pleasure craft driving license, and advanced diver and rescue diver certifications. The SCDF contingent was sent off by Assoc Prof Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim, Minister of State for the Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of National Development. We would like to thank Singapore Airlines for facilitating the flight arrangements on short notice. We wish our Operation Lionheart contingent a successful mission.

caption: Following the conclusion of a 24-hour assessment by a team of International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) assessors, we are pleased to announce that the SCDF Urban Search and Rescue (USAR) framework for our ORNS Rescue and Medical Units (RU/MU) has been successfully accredited! SCDF is honoured to be the first organisation in the Asia-Pacific region to undergo this accreditation exercise and have its USAR framework for ORNS units recognised by the INSARAG. About 300 ORNS personnel from the SCDF 21 RU/MU were involved in this accreditation exercise held at the Home Team Tactical Centre over the weekend, where their USAR capabilities were tested in both day and night operations involving complex height rescue, cutting, rigging and lifting operations. LTC (NS) Jahan De Silva Din Abdullah, Commander, 21 RU, was proud of his unit's effort and contributions in attaining this achievement for SCDF - Our training and hard work over the past three years, and overcoming the challenges posed by the pandemic, have come to fruition.Mr Mohd Halimi Taib, Team Lead of the Technical Recognition Group from INSARAG, complimented the ORNS Unit for having shown "a high level of competency and skills proficiency. This enabled the unit to have good command, control and coordination of the multiple and concurrent rescue and medical scenarios that the unit was tested over the 24-hour assessment". Our deep appreciation goes out to our ORNSmen without whom this achievement would not be possible. Thank you for your strong commitment in serving the nation! TheLifeSavingForce SCDFcelebratesNS55

caption: [SCDF Celebrates NS55]Meet LTA(Dr) Justin Ng Choon Hwee, a Medical Officer (MO) currently serving his full-time National Service with SCDF.As a MO, LTA(Dr) Justin's job scope includes conducting medical board reviews where he assesses SCDF officers' suitability to take on different frontline roles based on their fitness level. MOs are also part of the SCDF Operation Lionheart Contingent when it is activated for overseas humanitarian missions.In his seven months with the Force, LTA(Dr) Justin has seen through various projects, one of which was an initiative to improve Paramedic education and training. Through the development of a digital application to replace traditional pen and paper tests, data values and insights are obtained to provide real-time, customised feedback for Paramedics, thereby improving their learning experience. Here in SCDF, we are thankful for the diversity of our National Servicemen, together with their specialised skillsets and knowledge, for they help to propel innovation and performance in our everyday life.{Stay tuned for the coverage of more NS vocations in our subsequent series!}SCDFcelebratesNS55

caption: [Fire @ Kusu Island]At approximately 6.30pm yesterday on 17 April in the midst of a heavy downpour, SCDFs marine and land-based firefighting forces responded to a fire at Kusu island, one of the offshore islands on the southern coast of Singapore. SCDF despatched a Marine Rescue Vessel (MRV) and a Rapid Response Fire Vessel (RFV) from Brani Marine Fire Station and West Coast Marine Fire Station. An additional firefighting crew from Marina Bay Fire Station was also despatched and responded aboard the RFV. Upon SCDF's arrival at the island, the fire was raging at a cluster of shrines located on top of a hill. Using the MRV as a water pump, the firefighters laid a vast number of hoses from the jetty to the top of the hill, covering a distance of about 520 meters. The fire was extinguished with two water jets within an hour of SCDF's arrival on the island.There were no reported injuries. Damping down* operations are ongoing. The cause of the fire is under investigation. *Damping down refers to the application of water to burnt surfaces immediately after a fire is put out. It is to prevent any potential rekindling of fire from hot burnt surfaces.

caption: On 1 April 2022 at about 6.35am, SCDF was alerted to a road traffic accident near the junction of Lok Yang Way and First Lok Yang Road. Upon SCDF's arrival at the incident scene, a passenger bus was found overturned on its side. Another passenger bus had rammed into a fence by the roadside and a man was pinned in the driver's seat. Firefighters from Jurong Fire Station used hydraulic rescue equipment to free the man. The man was subsequently pronounced dead at the scene by an SCDF paramedic. As there were multiple casualties involved in this accident, the first-arriving SCDF paramedic established a triaging system to prioritise the casualties according to the severity of their injuries. Casualties with severe injuries were treated and conveyed to the hospitals as priority. Additional ambulances and medical resources were also dispatched to support the ongoing operation. A Mass Decontamination Vehicle (MDV) from SCDF's Special Rescue Unit (SRU) was also activated to the incident. Responders from the SRU, comprising Full-time National Servicemen, configured their MDV into a casualty conveyance vehicle. The MDV subsequently conveyed 14 casualties to Ng Teng Fong General Hospital.A total of 37 casualties were conveyed by SCDF to Ng Teng Fong General Hospital and National University Hospital.

caption: [Good Samaritans saved lives at Labrador Jetty and Kusu Island] On 1 Feb 2022, Mr Hadnan Bin Yaacob and Mr Mohammed Fazly Bin Ahmad Roslisham were at their family get-together at Labrador Park when a man fell into the sea from Labrador Jetty. Mr Hadnan and Mr Fazly immediately jumped into the water to rescue the unconscious man. Once on shore, Mr Hadnan commenced Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation (CPR) on the man who subsequently regained consciousness. On 12 Feb 2022, Mr Joaquin Sanchez and Mr Inigo Nicolas Ortiz were at Kusu Island when they heard shouts for help. Rushing towards the direction of the cries, they saw a floating figure in the sea. Without hesitation, Mr Joaquin and Mr Ortiz jumped into the sea and brought the unresponsive man back to shore. They commenced CPR on the man who subsequently regained his breathing. For their prompt life saving actions, the four Good Samaritans were each awarded with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award on 3 Mar 2022. The award was presented by COL Shaiful Herman Bin Shali, Commander, 1st SCDF Division. Kudos to these brave individuals who stepped forward to help others during an emergency situation! caption: You might have seen videos circulating online a few weeks ago of smoke billowing dramatically out from the SLE underpass. What you didn't see was the teamwork of a dynamic duo to save the day...On 2 November 2021, during the early evening rush hour traffic at about 5.00pm, two gentlemen rescued a driver from a car that was on fire at the exit 1 slip road of the underpass along SLE (towards BKE).One of these gentlemen, Mr Johnson Chia Yong Lee, was driving along SLE when he saw a car careen across the road and hit the left wall of the underpass. Mr Johnson opened the driver's door and swiftly brought the dazed driver out of the car. Another gentleman, Mr Azlee Bin Abd Shukor, was driving a van when he spotted black smoke and flames in the SLE underpass. Then, he saw Mr Johnson waving frantically for assistance. Realizing the precarious situation, he stopped his van alongside Mr Johnson.Working as a team, the duo brought the dazed driver into Mr Azlee's van. They then drove further down the road towards safety, away from the intense heat and smoke of the burning car.For their gallant rescue and timely intervention, Mr Johnson and Mr Azlee were each presented with the SCDF Community Lifesaver Award by COL Lim Beng Hui, Commander 3rd SCDF Division, today.Kudos to Mr Johnson and Mr Azlee, our brave heroes! caption: [SCDF conducts workshop on Urban Search and Rescue for international participants]Recently, SCDF, with support from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (UNOCHA), conducted a workshop on the International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG) Guidelines 2020 for the Asia Pacific (AP) region.The virtual event was attended by about 120 international participants from the INSARAG Network, including government officials and national civil defence organisations. The opening remarks were delivered by SCDFs Deputy Commissioner (Ops and Resilience), DC Anwar Abdullah, and the INSARAG AP Regional Chair 2021 from BASARNAS Indonesia, Mr Barokna Haulah. During the three-hour session, SCDF speakers introduced participants to the INSARAG community, its systems, and fundamentals of the latest Guidelines - a set of internationally accepted documents that outline the methodology for countries to develop their national urban search and rescue (USAR) response capability. The Guidelines also outline the requirements and standards for international USAR teams to respond to affected countries.The speakers also provided advice on developing a countrys national emergency management framework, which would allow them to better respond to disasters. The workshop concluded with a robust exchange of views during a Q&A session, where participants gleaned a deeper understanding on the practical applications of the Guidelines.We look forward to our continued partnership with the INSARAG network and stand ever ready to contribute to the international Search and Rescue community.

caption: [23rd Rota Commander Course (RCC) Commissioning Ceremony]This morning, 41 officer cadets from the 23rd Rota Commander Course (RCC) were commissioned as SCDF Senior Officers in a ceremony held at the Civil Defence Academy. At the closed-door ceremony due to the ongoing COVID-19 situation, family members and invited guests were able to tune into a live video broadcast of the ceremony to bear witness to this proud moment of their loved ones.The RCC commissioning ceremony is a significant milestone that marks the transition of officer cadets into Senior Officers after 28 weeks of rigorous training. As Senior Officers, these 15 career officers and 26 full-time national servicemen will be leading a team to respond to a wide multitude of firefighting and rescue incidents.In a virtual speech delivered by Mr. Desmond Tan, Minister of State (MOS) for Ministry of Home Affairs and Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment, he reiterated that while the COVID-19 pandemic has changed the way we go about our lives, SCDFs core function of firefighting, rescue and emergency medical services remain unchanged. He acknowledged that SCDF has employed new technologies in transforming its operations and emphasized the need to continue to do so, in order to remain effective and efficient.Congratulations to our newly commissioned SCDF Senior Officers! We wish them all the best as they go forth in their journey with the Life Saving Force. [Due to the COVID-19 pandemic, Safe Management Measures (SMM) were observed at the event to ensure the safety of all attendees.]ANationofLifesavers

caption: [SCDF X IBM Lifesavers' Innovation Challenge: Call for Code 2021 - Grand Finals] Yesterday, the Grand Finals of the SCDF X IBM Lifesavers' Innovation Challenge: Call for Code 2021, in partnership with Accenture, took place at the Marina Bay Sands Convention Centre. This annual event encourages members of the public to innovate solutions to tackle various issues relating to emergency response and civil defence in Singapore. This year, close to 225 students from local tertiary institutions formed teams to participate in the challenge. Before yesterdays event, teams were tasked to submit a 1-minute video pitch along with a code sequence to address one of the problem statements on a Post-Pandemic society, Sustainable Development, and Climate Change. Six teams eventually made it to todays Grand Finals. The six teams had to pitch their ideas to a panel of judges comprising SCDFs Deputy Commissioner (DC) Teong How Hwa, DC, Future Technology & Public Safety; Tan Jee Toon, Director of IBM Partner Ecosystem Leader (ASEAN); and Cade Tan, Applied Innovation & Ventures Lead (Accenture Southeast Asia). Congratulations to team 'Seviours' for emerging as this years champion! They have been awarded a cash prize of S$10,000 for their winning idea of a system that leverages Internet-of-Things (IoT) sensors, Artifical Intelligence (AI), and automation to enable early and efficient response to high-voltage charging fires. Four other teams were awarded a total cash prize of S$11,000. Each of the top five teams was also awarded up to US$120,000 in IBM cloud credits to develop their projects with IBM. A big thank you to all participants! As we head towards a decade of new frontiers, our civil defence, community resilience and emergency response will need to keep up with the times. Now more than ever, we need innovative solutions so that as ANationOfLifesavers, we are always ready to respond.[In light of the COVID-19 pandemic, Safe Management Measures (SMM) were observed at the event to ensure the safety of all attendees.]

caption: [Workers commended for rescuing boy from ledge]You may have seen a recent viral video of a worker operating a boom lift to rescue a boy from a kitchen ledge. Today, SCDF awarded him and his colleague for their heroic act.On Sunday morning (3 Jan), Mr Das Dipto, a landscape maintenance worker, was cleaning a boom lift which he had used for pruning trees when an anxious woman approached him and his colleague, Mr Biswas Jibom. The woman pleaded for them to help a boy who was stranded on a third-floor kitchen ledge at a nearby HDB block 243, Hougang Street 22. With Mr Jibom directing him and ensuring the path ahead was clear, Mr Dipto carefully steered the machinery with the boom lift down a narrow pathtowards the block. He saw the frightful boy precariously standing on the ledge, crying and grabbing onto a laundry pole. Mr Dipto raised the boom lifts platform towards the boy while calmly assuring the boy that he was there to rescue him. Within minutes, Mr Dipto reached out with both his arms, lifted the boy onto the platform and lowered him to safety, much to the relief and rousing cheers from a crowd of onlookers.When SCDF resources arrived, the boy had already been rescued. He was assessed by an SCDF paramedic and he did not require any medical assistance.Today, for their quick-thinking and selfless act, Mr Dipto and Mr Jibom received SCDF's Community Lifesaver Award from COL Lim Han Chee, 3rd SCDF Division Commander.Thank you Mr Dipto and Mr Jibom! Your commendable act brings us closer to building ANationOfLifesavers.

caption: On 27 September, a man was found unconscious near Boon Lay MRT station. Suspecting that the man had suffered a cardiac arrest, four Community First Responders (CFRs) responded swiftly and worked together to save the man. Off-duty nurse from National University Hospital (NUH), Ms. Franchesca Santos Rubio, was alerted of the incident via the myResponder app and rushed to the location from her home. She immediately performed one cycle of CPR on the man. Two SMRT staff, Mr. Muhammad Azhari bin Abdullah and Mdm. Hilmiah Binte Ahmad also assisted by bringing an AED and placing the pads on the man. Mdm. Hilmiah subsequently administered three AED shocks.SMRTs Mr. Baharudin Bin Johan presence was also timely in helping to manage the crowd. This allowed the CFRs to have the working space needed to safely administer CPR and use the AED. All four CFRs remained by the mans side until the arrival of SCDFs emergency medical services.On Monday, for their gallant efforts in helping to save a life, Ms. Franchesca and Mdm. All four CFRs remained by the man's side until the arrival of SCDF's emergency medical services. On Monday, for their gallant efforts in helping to save a life, the off-duty nurse and the other staff member were awarded with the Community Lifesaver Award while the remaining staff members were awarded with the Community First Responder Award.
